relevance_note: Describes one index case with LCAT variants and Fish Eye Disease, plus tested relatives: 'one IC with a compound heterozygosity in LCAT causing Fish Eye Disease'.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; a short Python script assembled the JSON (no table transcription by script). Seven index cases in a low-HDL/low-LDL lipid cohort; only Index case 2 carries LCAT variants (the other six have ABCA1, APOB or no variant and are out of scope; counted in cohort_size_as_stated). Label 'Index case 2' is the case-report heading (also 'IC2' in Figure 2 legend and ID 2 in Table 1). Relatives: the text names 'the father' (HDL 29 mg/dl), the other parent only as one of 'the parents' (sex not stated, so labelled 'parent of Index case 2', not 'mother'), and 'the sister' (non-carrier). Each parent carries one of the two LCAT variants ('inherited a different variant from each parent'), but the text does not say which parent carries which (only Figure 2, not available), so the parents' variant rows have variant_original_string 'not reported' and zygosity/pathogenicity left 'not reported'; IC2's inheritance is 'inherited unspecified parent'. Transcript NM_000229 is taken from the Methods list of references given 'respectively' for ABCA1, APOA1, LCAT, ...; it is not printed next to the variants. 'Suspected Fish-eye-disease since the age of 45' is a suspected diagnosis, not recorded as age at diagnosis (Discussion says only 'the diagnosis was only made later in life'). Table 1 numeric values for IC2 (TC 108, LDL-C 31, HDL-C 12, TGs 98, ApoA1 41, ApoB 61 mg/dl) are not labelled low/high by the paper and were not used to mark checklist items (e.g. low apoA-I, low LDL left not reported). Possible inconsistencies: Table 1 TGs 98 mg/dl vs text 'hypertriglyceridemia (158–263 mg/dl)' (patient on fibrates; not treated as a contradiction); the road accident is dated 2008 in the case text but 'At 35 years old' in the Discussion; corneal opacification is 'revealed' at ophthalmology in the case text but 'since childhood' in the Discussion. The statement that kidney disease is not associated with FED is general and was not used to exclude CKD; the non-functioning right kidney is post-traumatic. The other parent's low HDL comes from the named-group statement 'the IC parents have low HDL values' (evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement').
